summary.text:
Global equities were mixed as European and Asian markets advanced, supported by easing trade tensions and China's October industrial profits surging 20.1%. The DAX climbed 2.08% and the Nikkei 225 rose 1.85%. In the US, the Dow gained 0.33%, while the Nasdaq dropped 0.64% as Nvidia fell 3.91% despite Singapore not confirming halted chip shipments. A fatal Kuwait drone attack also drew geopolitical attention.

The US dollar index rose 0.14% to 103.81, with EURUSD at 1.0976. Gold advanced 2.39% to 3620.3999. In commodities, WTI crude added 0.88% to 84.42, while Brent tumbled 3.64% to 91.17. Bitcoin gained 1.75% to 61433.7891, and equity volatility receded with the VIX falling 5.27% to 26.8.

Looking ahead, market participants are monitoring the IMF urging the Reserve Bank of Australia to maintain its monetary tightening bias, the market reaction to Brazil's new finance minister appointment, and developments in Middle East tensions.
